title: Etale localization of the algebraic-space naive cotangent complex
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Consider a commutative square of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with maps $f:X\to Y$, $g:U\to V$, $p:U\to X$, $q:V\to Y$ satisfying $fp=qg$, and assume $p$ and $q$ are etale. Here etale for maps of algebraic spaces means representable and etale on scheme base changes, using [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No cartesian-square hypothesis is imposed. For the naive cotangent complexes [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex], there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq\mathrm{NL}_{U/V}\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_U)$$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where the left side is restriction along the etale localization of the small etale site.

proof.text:
Use the canonical small-etale ringed topoi and their composition comparisons from [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Since $p$ and $q$ are etale, their morphisms are localizations, with $p^{-1}\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_U$ and $q^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\cong\mathcal O_V$ as structure rings. The equality $fp=qg$ therefore gives an isomorphism of ring-sheaf maps
$$(p^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to p^{-1}\mathcal O_X)\cong(g^{-1}\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal O_U).$$
Compatibility of the arrows follows from compatibility of composition as ringed topoi: both arrows are pullback of regular functions along $U\to Y$. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], restriction along the localized site is exact on module sheaves, so termwise restriction represents the restriction of the derived object.

source.place: Tag 0D0W, lemma-NL-etale-localization, proof; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LV, lemma-etale-exact-pullback.

proof.text:
Put $A=f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$ and $B=\mathcal O_X$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. The definition [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex] gives $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}=\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$. Apply [lem-sfb-topos-naive-cotangent-pullback] to the geometric inverse image $p^{-1}$ and this map of ring sheaves. Using step 1 to identify the coefficient ring, this gives
$$\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq\mathrm{NL}_{p^{-1}\mathcal O_X/p^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_U).$$
This is an isomorphism of the derived complexes, not just of their cohomology sheaves.

Substitute the isomorphism of ring-sheaf maps from step 1 into the right side of step 2. In the standard presentation, coefficients and variables are renamed by those ring isomorphisms, evaluation is preserved, and $[h]\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1$ becomes the same differential for $g^{-1}\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal O_U$. This identifies that complex with $\mathrm{NL}_{U/V}$ by [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex]. Composing gives the required canonical isomorphism. Only commutativity $fp=qg$ was used; the square need not be cartesian.
